item_verdicts.manifest: read at the run directory; status complete, commits 429584af8 and c121df9cb named, checkpoint records the worktree clean at c121df9cb, three gate logs named and on disk, negative_control_log carries the bare path with its declared mutation, and the baseline_suite/after_suite fields are armed JSON with revision, command, exit_status, completed, failure_count and failure_ids present.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed manifest declares five write paths (reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/cli.py, tests/test_member_friction.py, the evidence fragment, a figures directory); the final diff touches three of them — dispatch.py, the new test file and the fragment — and every changed path is inside the declaration, with reckon/cli.py and the figures path left unwritten and no path outside the reviewed node's own files.

justifications.durability: the new test file drives both directions of the guard — the resolving case and the refusing case — against a synthesised temporary checkout and a temporary configuration home, and it asserts the real pointer directory and every real roster are byte-identical before and after, which is the write-side isolation the repository's rules require; the negative control shows the cases redden when the fix is removed, so the guard demonstrably fires; held back one because the guard delegates entirely to resolve_project_repository, already covered by the suite whose call sites the change does not itself re-assert.
justifications.evidence: the two-arm gate and the negative control are recorded with their own revision/tree/command headers and reproduce — this review re-ran the head arm at c121df9cb (46 passed, EXIT=0) and the negative-control log reddens exactly the two guarded cases (2 failed / 1 passed, EXIT=1) that the head arm fails neither; docked because both the reviewed after_suite revision field and the head-arm.log revision header name the base revision 33c5e761d (the header qualifying it as a working-tree repair) rather than the committed repair 429584af8 or the final head, so the run's own record does not tie its head count to the revision the change sits at.
justifications.fit: the repair reuses the existing resolve_project_repository with its default --repo flag rather than adding a second resolution path, so the validating and launching answers converge on one decision; the inline comment states the mechanism; the test module follows the repository's synthesised-repository and temporary-config-home idiom and names its helpers by what they do; the docstring's references to the frictions are descriptive prose rather than plan labels.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the goal is met at c121df9cb: a lane-naming member dispatch with repo=None resolves the project's registered mount and passes validation (authority write repository equals the mount), while an unmounted project still refuses with the fix's own message naming --repo; the second friction is correctly measured as already-correct and kept as a guard, and no part of the required behaviour is missing.
justifications.scope_discipline: the changed set is three paths, all inside the five-path declaration; the worktree is clean at the reviewed head; the two commits carry conventional subjects and bodies with no plan, sprint or ticket identifiers and no attribution; and the manifest discloses, rather than claims, the two declared paths it did not write.
